name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2G

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2G

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in lower limbs with distal sensory loss
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes and normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities
Identification of pathogenic heterozygous mutations in the HSPB1 gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Muscle biopsy showing neurogenic atrophy (if performed)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical neuropathy, electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy, and pathogenic HSPB1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential due to phenotypic overlap with other CMT subtypes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Distal sensory loss affecting vibration and proprioception
searchTerms: loss of vibration and position sense in feet
reduced ability to feel vibrations distally
impaired proprioception in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in lower limbs

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop
muscle cramps in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Reduced pinprick sensation in distal extremities
searchTerms: reduced sharp pain feeling in fingers and toes
less sensitivity to pinprick in extremities
nerve pain in hands and feet
burning or shooting pain in limbs
pain from nerve damage in extremities
hands and feet sensitive to cold
cold intolerance in fingers and toes
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of neuropathy
imaging: Muscle MRI may show fatty infiltration in distal muscles (research setting)
genetic: Pathogenic heterozygous mutations in HSPB1 gene (heat shock protein beta-1)
other: Nerve conduction studies showing axonal neuropathy pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Transient nerve palsies triggered by compression

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
Respiratory compromise or vocal cord paralysis
references: Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
